projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The consistently high device count (15-18) on a Sunday evening, paired with no camera alerts, indicates a planned social gathering or family visit is underway. This context explains the active home environment and helps distinguish normal occupancy from potential security events.

The rapid fluctuation in high mobile device counts (17–22) combined with zero camera activity strongly indicates a network artifact (likely IoT devices or Wi-Fi scanning) rather than actual human occupancy, which could cause false presence-based automations.

Connected mobile devices gradually declined from 22 to 18 over two hours while cameras recorded no motion, suggesting the household may be packing up or leaving with devices going offline or moving out of range. This is likely normal weekend behavior, but worth noting to confirm departure status.

The device count increased to 23 at 01:29 AM and has remained completely stable for over an hour with zero camera, light, or water activity, indicating a single device was brought indoors and left stationary—likely a guest or late-arriving household member who went directly to a bedroom without triggering other sensors.

At 01:29 AM, the connected mobile device count increased from 22 to 23 with no corresponding camera or audio activity, suggesting a single device (likely a phone or tablet) woke up or reconnected while the rest of the household remained asleep.

The sustained 19–22 connected devices paired with zero camera motion alerts strongly indicates a settled indoor social gathering (likely guests) rather than an empty or unoccupied home, confirming normal Saturday evening activity.

The stable count of 20-22 mobile devices on a Saturday evening, paired with zero camera alerts, strongly indicates a planned social gathering or family visit rather than a system anomaly. Recognizing this pattern prevents unnecessary alerts and confirms the home is hosting guests safely.

The presence count has stabilized at 20-22 devices for the past hour with zero camera alerts, confirming the initial guest surge has settled into a stable indoor gathering. This cross-signal pattern indicates a normal Saturday evening event with no recent departures or outdoor activity, so no action is needed.

A sudden surge to 22 connected devices at 16:58, followed by a gradual decline, strongly indicates a large group of guests has arrived, which is highly unusual for the household size. Since no camera activity was recorded during this arrival window, verify that visitors are accounted for and that entry points remain secure.

The presence count dropped from 14 to 12 devices between 15:04 and 15:14, indicating two people likely departed, but the lack of camera activity suggests they exited via a non-covered entry or cameras are inactive. This is a normal Saturday routine, but the cross-signal gap is worth noting for complete home monitoring.
